hints: Remember to divide by the coefficient of $x$ (which is $4$) when integrating.
Substitute $(2, 5)$ into the integrated expression to find $c$.
walkthrough:
Express the derivative in index form and set up the indefinite integral:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 8(4x + 1)^{-1/2} \implies y = \int 8(4x + 1)^{-1/2}\,dx$$

Integrate using the reverse chain rule for linear composite functions, including $+ c$:
$$y = 8 \times \frac{(4x + 1)^{1/2}}{\frac{1}{2} \times 4} + c = 4\sqrt{4x + 1} + c$$

Substitute $x = 2$ and $y = 5$ into the equation to find $c$:
$$5 = 4\sqrt{4(2) + 1} + c \implies 5 = 4(3) + c \implies 5 = 12 + c \implies c = -7$$

State the complete equation of the curve:
$$y = 4\sqrt{4x + 1} - 7$$
